clips.text: You type six words, hit Enter, and a whole website appears. Here's the journey behind that.
First, your browser has to find where that domain actually points.
It asks DNS for the right address, like looking up a contact before calling.
Next, your browser opens a connection to that server.
For a secure site, it also sets up an encrypted HTTPS connection.
Then it sends a request: please give me this page.
The server replies with data: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, or links to more files.
Your browser reads those pieces and builds the page you see.
That is why a page can look broken while the server responds fine: one image failed to load.
So the short version: find the address, connect, request, receive, render. Next time you type a URL, you'll see the whole journey.
